newsitem.title: USA: U.S. grain dealers taking 5-10 cts protection soy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grain dealers taking 5-10 cts protection soy.

text.p: U.S. Midwest grain dealers said they were taking scattered protection of five to ten cents per bushel on new crop soybeans in anticipation of a lower open on the CBOT.
"We're taking a dime again on new-crop beans," said one Illinois river dealer.
CBOT November soybean futures were expected to open as much as 10 cents lower following a limit-down close on Monday.
Soybeans fell sharply Monday in response to data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture that forecast the largest soybean crop in 15 years.
USDA estimated the 1997/98 (Aug/Sep) soybean crop at 70.9 million acres.
